options.summary: Monolithic CLI pipeline in Node.js – a single CLI tool orchestrates all stages (parse, link-resolve, index-build, render) in one sequential build process, outputting a complete static site. Uses unified/remark for Markdown, Lunr.js for client-side search index generation, and a built-in template engine (e.g., Nunjucks) for HTML rendering.

components.name: CLI Entry Point
responsibilities: Parse command-line arguments (input folder, output folder, config file path)
Orchestrate the build pipeline stages in sequence
Report build progress and errors to stdout/stderr

components.name: Markdown Parser & Frontmatter Extractor
responsibilities: Read all .md files from the input directory tree
Parse YAML frontmatter to extract tags and metadata
Parse Markdown AST using unified/remark
Detect and normalize internal links (standard Markdown links and wiki-links)

components.name: Link & Backlink Resolver
responsibilities: Build a forward-link graph from parsed internal links
Compute the inverse graph to derive backlinks for every note
Resolve link targets to output URLs
Report broken/unresolvable links as warnings

components.name: Tag Index Builder
responsibilities: Aggregate tags across all notes
Generate per-tag note lists
Produce a global tag index data structure for tag browsing pages

components.name: Search Index Generator
responsibilities: Build a Lunr.js (or FlexSearch) index from note titles, content, and tags at build time
Serialize the index to a JSON file included in the static output
Keep index size manageable via stop-word removal and stemming

components.name: HTML Renderer / Templating Engine
responsibilities: Convert Markdown AST to HTML
Inject backlinks, tag lists, and navigation into page templates
Render tag index pages, home page, and search page
Copy static assets (CSS, JS, images) to output directory

components.name: Client-Side Search UI
responsibilities: Load the pre-built search index in the browser
Provide a search input with real-time results
Highlight matched terms in result snippets

interfaces.contract: Passes resolved input directory path and config object (Markdown flavor, link syntax options) to the parser.
Emits an array of NoteRecord objects: {slug, title, frontmatter, markdownAST, rawLinks[{target, anchor, type}]}.
Emits an array of NoteRecord objects with extracted tags: {slug, tags[]}.
Provides a Map<slug, BacklinkEntry[]> where BacklinkEntry = {sourceSlug, sourceTitle, context}.
Provides a Map<tag, slug[]> for tag index pages and per-note tag links.
Provides an array of {slug, title, plainTextContent, tags[]} for indexing.
Outputs a serialized search index JSON file path to be included in site assets.
The rendered search page loads the search index JSON and the client-side JS bundle via <script> tags.

pros: Simple single-process build; easy to reason about and debug
Minimal external dependencies; one npm install
Fast for small-to-medium note sets (hundreds of notes)
Straightforward deployment: run CLI, upload output folder
cons: Monolithic codebase may become hard to extend with new features (graph view, themes)
Full rebuild required on any change (no incremental builds)
Lunr.js index can become large for thousands of notes, increasing page load time
Tightly coupled components make it harder to swap individual parts (e.g., replace search engine)

risks: Search index JSON may exceed acceptable download size for very large note sets (1000+ notes), degrading first-load performance
Wiki-link syntax ambiguity (e.g., Obsidian vs. other dialects) may cause incorrect link resolution without clear spec
Single-threaded sequential build may become slow for very large repositories

options.summary: Plugin-based static site generator architecture – a lightweight core orchestrator with a formal plugin API. Each concern (Markdown parsing, backlinks, tags, search) is a separate plugin conforming to a shared hook contract. Enables swapping or extending functionality (e.g., different search backends, theme plugins) without modifying core.

components.name: Core Orchestrator & Plugin Host
responsibilities: Load configuration and discover/register plugins
Define build lifecycle hooks (init, collectFiles, transform, resolve, render, finalize)
Execute plugins in defined hook order
Manage shared build context (note registry, site metadata)

components.name: File Collector Plugin
responsibilities: Recursively scan input directory for Markdown files
Emit file metadata into the shared note registry
Support configurable file include/exclude patterns

components.name: Markdown Parser Plugin
responsibilities: Parse each Markdown file into an AST (using unified/remark or markdown-it)
Extract YAML frontmatter
Normalize internal link references into a canonical format

components.name: Backlink Resolver Plugin
responsibilities: Subscribe to the resolve hook
Build forward-link and backlink graphs from parsed link data
Attach backlink metadata to each note in the registry

components.name: Tag Aggregator Plugin
responsibilities: Collect tags from frontmatter and/or inline #tag syntax
Build tag-to-notes index
Register tag index pages for rendering

components.name: Search Index Plugin
responsibilities: Build a client-side search index (Lunr, FlexSearch, or Pagefind)
Serialize index artifacts to the output directory
Optionally support chunked/sharded indexes for large sites

components.name: Theme / Renderer Plugin
responsibilities: Provide HTML templates and CSS/JS assets
Render each note, tag page, index page, and search page using the build context
Support theme switching via configuration

components.name: Client-Side Runtime
responsibilities: Load and query the search index in the browser
Render interactive search results
Provide tag filter UI and backlink navigation

interfaces.contract: Hook: collectFiles(context) → context.noteRegistry populated with {filePath, slug} entries.
Hook: transform(context) → each noteRegistry entry enriched with {ast, frontmatter, rawLinks[]}.
Hook: resolve(context) → context.backlinkMap: Map<slug, BacklinkEntry[]> attached.
Hook: resolve(context) → context.tagIndex: Map<tag, slug[]> attached.
Hook: finalize(context) → search index files written to context.outputDir/search/.
Hook: render(context) → HTML files written to context.outputDir using templates + context data.
Rendered HTML pages reference client-side JS bundle and search index assets via relative paths.

pros: Highly extensible: new features added as plugins without touching core
Themes are swappable; community can contribute plugins
Concerns are cleanly separated, improving testability
Search backend can be swapped (Lunr vs. Pagefind) via plugin config
cons: More upfront design and implementation effort for the plugin API
Plugin ordering and hook dependencies add complexity
Debugging cross-plugin issues can be harder than a monolith
Over-engineering risk for a small-scope project

risks: Plugin API design may need multiple iterations to stabilize, delaying initial delivery
Poorly documented plugin contracts could lead to brittle third-party plugins
Performance overhead from plugin hook dispatch may matter at scale

options.summary: Leverage an existing static site generator (e.g., Eleventy/11ty) as the build engine with custom plugins/filters for backlinks, tags, and search. Reduces custom code by reusing a mature SSG's file handling, templating, and incremental build capabilities.

components.name: Eleventy (11ty) Core Engine
responsibilities: Handle file discovery, templating, and static output generation
Provide data cascade and collections API for structured data
Support incremental builds and watch mode out of the box

components.name: Markdown Processing Configuration
responsibilities: Configure markdown-it (or remark via plugin) with desired Markdown flavor
Add wiki-link syntax support via markdown-it plugin
Extract frontmatter automatically via Eleventy data cascade

components.name: Backlink Data Plugin (Eleventy Plugin)
responsibilities: Run as an Eleventy addCollection or computed data step
Scan all note collections for internal links
Compute and inject backlink data into each note's template data

components.name: Tag Collection & Pages
responsibilities: Use Eleventy's built-in tag collection mechanism
Generate per-tag index pages via pagination templates
Provide tag cloud / tag list data to templates

components.name: Search Index Build Step
responsibilities: Use eleventy-plugin-pagefind or a custom afterBuild event to generate a search index
Pagefind indexes the rendered HTML output for accurate full-text search
Output search UI assets alongside the site

components.name: Theme / Layout Templates
responsibilities: Provide Nunjucks/Liquid templates for note pages, tag pages, home, and search
Include CSS framework or custom styles
Render backlink sections and tag links within templates

components.name: Pagefind Client-Side Search
responsibilities: Provide a lightweight JS widget that loads chunked search index on demand
Support instant search with highlighting
No custom search UI code needed beyond configuration

interfaces.contract: Eleventy config registers markdown-it library with wiki-link plugin; .md files processed automatically.
Eleventy addCollection('backlinks', ...) callback receives all note collection items with their template content and parsed links.
Each note's data object includes a backlinks[] array: {slug, title, excerpt} available in templates.
Eleventy collections.tagList and collections[tagName] auto-populated from frontmatter tags field.
Eleventy afterBuild event triggers Pagefind indexing on the _site output directory.
Pagefind outputs chunked index files and a pagefind-ui.js bundle into _site/pagefind/; search page includes <link> and <script> references.
Templates registered in Eleventy config via addLayoutAlias and directory data files.

pros: Dramatically less custom code; leverages battle-tested SSG
Incremental builds and watch mode available out of the box
Pagefind provides chunked search indexes that scale to thousands of pages
Large Eleventy ecosystem and community for support and extensions
cons: Tied to Eleventy's conventions and release cycle
Backlink computation requires custom plugin code that must integrate with Eleventy's data model
Less control over build pipeline internals compared to a fully custom solution
Eleventy upgrade or breaking changes could require migration effort

risks: Eleventy's data cascade may introduce unexpected behavior for large or deeply nested note structures
Pagefind dependency adds an external binary (Rust-based); may complicate CI/CD on some platforms
Wiki-link resolution in markdown-it plugin may not cover all edge cases without significant customization
